stage: Canonical remaster, concept and independent imported-GLB feedback reviewed

iterations.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: OpenFA Artemian Hardcore AR4C, large ore/missile transporter remaster. Attached reference is ACTUAL paletted legacy headings0/4/12/28 and primary authority. Same silhouette: TWO rounded flattened gold/brown pressure hull bodies INLINE one behind the other along the craft's fore-aft axis, connected by an exposed shorter SILVER METAL bridge/spine. NOT side-by-side, not a single long capsule. Each main body has TWO small gold/brown lateral modules, one to port and one starboard, on short structural arms; four small side modules TOTAL. Modest gold tail plane behind rear hull, small blue-grey fore service interface and two slender blue-grey aft projections, matching the source cues. Main bodies are low convex domed/rounded alloy volumes with flattened lower lobes, a broad equatorial seam, NOT perfect balls. Entire assembly reads as a low industrial cargo spacecraft. Shared Artemian metal/alloy style but preserve this ship's warm BRONZE/GOLD body palette, silver bridge and sparse blue-grey details, no green replacement hull. Five equipment slots exist but mount positions/functions are unknown: do not invent engines/guns/cockpits or emission. Bright source marks are reflections, not evidence of lights/windows. No cargo containers, cranes, antenna dish, extra bodies, big fins or fantasy additions. Readable high-detail practical game remaster with sparse fitted maintenance covers, shallow slots, small seated fasteners and structural trims. No dense rectangular hull panel grid; broad calm shell surfaces. Appropriate use wear: restrained grime at joins, irregular stains, scuffs, small scratches and tiny dents, not pristine or wrecked. Show one coherent craft in large front three-quarter view, smaller true side and top views with exactly the same body count and arm/module layout. Plain charcoal studio background, no labels, logos or text.
iterations.verdict: Retained broad reference: two inline warm-metal rounded bodies, silver bridge, four small lateral modules on short arms, small aft plane and blue-grey details. Exact bridge machinery, collars, fore-interface length, hatch/trim shapes remain artistic interpretation; actual legacy takes precedence.

glb_feedback.verdict: Actual imported hero/side/end views preserve the warm twin-body layout and silver bridge. The comparison camera reversed fore/aft relative to AR4C and was too elevated for the thin side heading. Rejected those comparison directions; do not distort the asset to compensate.

Estimated comparison azimuth changed from180 to0 degrees and elevation from.25 to.12; independently imported GLB rerendered and inspected against actual0/4/12/28 and concept1. Blue-grey fore interface now matches the correct visible end. Retained original fitted service details rather than copying speculative concept bridge mechanisms or enlarged fore fairing. 49716tri/4batches/1material,48editablepartgroups,51 tested contacts and six protected radial dents. Exact hidden geometry, body spacing and module engineering remain authored interpretation.

glb_visual_review: Actual 0/4/12/28 comparison inspected against correctly paletted legacy and concept1. Two rounded warm-metal bodies inline, exposed silver connector, four smaller lateral modules and aft plane/blue-grey details agree in broad silhouette and colour. The first source had an overly plain finish; remaster adds restrained worn PBR metal and softened service-cover/tail edges without dense panel grids. Original source fine geometry is retained where the concept invents extra bridge/fore-interface machinery. Reference side alpha122x18 and estimated comparison azimuth0/elevation.12 are not recovered client calibration or percentage fidelity. Highlights are not used to invent emission.
next_step: Use one canonical GLB across gameplay, ship/build menus and SciTek; validate WorldSize96 proposal, heading/materials and five uncalibrated equipment slots in client. Final user artistic acceptance separate.
